ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 cancellation charge to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7).
ruling.reasoning:
This is a driver-cancellation no-show case, so it enters the NS group through NS-0, which branches a driver-side cancellation asserting rider no-show into NS-1/NS-2 [F4]. The trace settles NS-1(i), (ii) and (iii): the driver tapped "I'm Here" (driver_tap, not a platform auto-confirmation) at 09:07:15 while 40 m from the pickup, closest approach 32 m [F6][F1][F5], but the continuous time inside the 200 m radius after that tap was 470 s against the case record's 8-minute (480 s) threshold, i.e. the wait fell short [F6][F2]. Because NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) must all hold and (iii) fails, no $5.00 no-show charge is due and the amount already taken must go back [F7][F4][NS-1][NS-2][NS-7].

The "? " element I must decide is the SAFE-1 screen. I read both chat messages and the driver's statement in context: F9 is an arrival announcement ("I'm here at the pickup point, white Honda Vezel"), F10 is a cancellation notice ("8 min up, cancelling the trip"), F12 is the driver's post-trip justification [F9][F10][F12]. Nothing in these, nor in the rider's complaint, is a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so I find safety_concern = none [F9][F10][F11][F12][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. The chat record is complete with every message timestamped [F11], the GPS trace runs from the arrival confirmation to the cancellation without a hole [F2][F3], the rider's own position at the moment of cancellation is something the complaint asserts but the record does not carry; as NS-1 (iii) is measured by the driver's elapsed time in the radius — which code has measured and settled — that absence does not leave any element of my ruling undetermined [F3][F6][NS-4].

Two rider-side arguments fall away: the conflicting-threshold point C2/C3 is withdrawn in the rider's own rebuttal, and the $5.00-vs-$6.61 label point is immaterial because the driver-side branch is priced from the case record's fee figure [F7]. The amount follows the trace's formula directly: the cancellation fee actually charged and on record is $5.00, and it is refunded in full [F7][F4][NS-2][NS-7].

On the account question: NS-2's flag arises only where the driver confirmed arrival while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius at that moment; here the tap was 40 m from the pickup, so no fake confirmation occurred and no flag is warranted [F1][F6][NS-2]. Nor does RD-6 bite — it concerns route disputes, and the driver has no upheld route dispute (route: 0) [F17][RD-6]. I accordingly do not set the account flag. The rider's requested flag on the driver's 4.48 rating and single prior upheld no-show is a profile-based ask, and profile facts cannot decide a case; they carry no weight in this outcome [F16][F17][RD-6]. The driver's argument that notice via F9/F10 legitimised the charge is rejected because NS-1 imposes no notice duty but does impose the wait threshold, and notice cannot cure a short wait [F9][F10][NS-1].

rejected_claims.reason: Fuses two different measures: 7 min 50 s (F6) is time inside the radius after the 09:07:15 tap, while 8 min 45 s (F2) is cumulative time inside the radius counted from 09:06:20 (F5). Only the continuous wait after the arrival confirmation counts under NS-1(iii), and code measures it at 470 s against the 480 s threshold — the segment is generous to the driver and fails.

Relies on F5/F12 for an 8-minute threshold being 'reached', but the trace's NS-1(iii) element is measured from the driver_tap and fails (470 s < 480 s) (F6); the driver's own statement in F12 is a claim, not consent or a system record, and cannot supply the missing wait.
Notice is not an element of NS-1: the clause requires a correct arrival tap plus the qualifying wait. The messages at F9 and F10 do not cure the short post-tap wait and create no basis to charge.
Asserts the $5.00 (F7) is a validated waiting/no-show charge; F8's absence of surge only shows the amount was not inflated, not that NS-1(iii) was met, which the trace settles as failed (F6, NS-1).

Raised to resist an account flag; correctly noted that the driver does not meet a 'repeated' pattern (route: 0, F17), which is why no flag is set — but profile facts cannot themselves decide the fee outcome (RD-6).
Withdrawn by the rider advocate in rebuttal; on the record the post-tap wait (470 s) is below the 480 s threshold, so the threshold is not met (F6, NS-1).

The NS-6 route fails: NS-6 governs a post-trip $5.00 waiting fee after the rider boards and the trip continues, and here the trip was cancelled before boarding (F4). The correct route is the driver-cancellation branch NS-0/NS-1/NS-2.
Asks the judge to weigh the rider's long clean account (F16) against the driver's prior upheld no-show (F17); profile facts may never decide a case and are not the basis of my outcome (RD-6).
